trigger: The ten-cluster gravity-flow inversion found that R50 and R50/R80 strongly track the inferred inward-return fraction, while the earlier scalar arc-apogee sweep showed that radial strength alone drifts back toward the MOND mass scale. This stage tests the distinct two-dimensional route geometry on raw image families.
question: Can one baryon-derived extent gate and one shared return geometry improve held-out raw image-plane consistency in both SMACS0723 and SPT0615 without using either cluster's reconstructed halo map to place endpoints?

formula.concentration: C=R50/R80 from hard-member F160W weights about the frozen lens-map origin, matching the ten-cluster inverse driver definition; routes point toward the weighted light centroid

route_modes.chord: deposit uniformly along the launch-to-return chord
route_modes.radial_arc_0.5: deposit along a path with a 0.5*R80 outward radial bow
route_modes.transverse_arc_0.5: split the route equally over opposite transverse bows of height 0.5*R80 so no handedness is inserted

formula.field: ordinary two-dimensional Poisson deflection; no fractional propagator
formula.conservation: Every local and routed surface is separately normalized; the kernel redistributes normalized source weight rather than creating map-integrated weight.

primary_inverse_candidate.selection_role: locked replay of the inverse-derived values; it is scored whether or not calibration selects it

selection.rule: Fit one positive normalization per cluster on its frozen calibration image families for each candidate. Select the minimum equal-cluster mean linearized image-plane RMS. Freeze that candidate and both normalizations before scoring every held-out family.

gates.solar_limit: An isolated point has R50=R80=0 and the route collapses to its launch point, giving exactly no force change.
gates.galaxy_limit: The same conservative radial redistribution is evaluated separately on SPARC after this raw-cluster selection; no galaxy null is assumed.

claim_limits: Hard-member F160W light is a stellar-light proxy and omits hot gas, intracluster light, and mass-to-light variation.
One amplitude per cluster remains calibrated, so this is a route-geometry test rather than an absolute-strength prediction.
The two clusters are fresh to the inverse-derived extent relation but have been used in P0573-P0578 formula work.
The linearized image-plane diagnostic is not a full nonlinear root solution.
Two clusters and five held-out subfamilies are insufficient to confirm a universal route law.
Projected path residence cannot determine an off-plane arc height or propagation time.
